objective:
Issue #29 (data side): every snapshot carries `demoPlannedAt`, the ISO UTC timestamp of today's planned demo recording start: DEMO_TIME (HH:MM, 24-hour) in DEMO_TZ (IANA zone) on the snapshot's `date`. The page will print it as "Demos are scheduled to run every day at 4:00 PM CST." while no demo has run.
1. In src/fetch/demo.ts add an exported pure function `plannedAt(date: string, env: Env): string | null`: time = env.DEMO_TIME || "16:00", zone = env.DEMO_TZ || "America/Chicago" (an empty string means the default, because an unset Actions variable arrives as ""). It returns the UTC instant whose wall-clock time in `zone` on `date` is `time`, e.g. ("2026-11-18", defaults) -> "2026-11-18T22:00:00.000Z" (CST) and ("2026-07-15", defaults) -> "2026-07-15T21:00:00.000Z" (CDT). Use Intl only (no new dependency). It returns null when DEMO_TIME doesn't match /^([01]\d|2[0-3]):[0-5]\d$/, when the zone is not a valid IANA zone (Intl throws RangeError), or when the wall-clock time doesn't exist that day (spring-forward gap, e.g. 2027-03-14 02:30 America/Chicago). In the fall-back hour (ambiguous), pick the earlier instant.
2. scripts/snapshot.ts sets `demoPlannedAt` from plannedAt(date, process.env). When it returns null, omit the field and print one warning line naming the bad variable or the gap (the Demo workflow's plan job already fails loudly on bad config; a snapshot must still be written, P-2).
Nothing else changes; no page text (P-1).
